structure:
repos/trade-imports-plants-frontend is the high-risk plants notification frontend (Node, Hapi, Nunjucks, GOV.UK Frontend) on the shared journey platform. The set mounts through src/server/app/routes-high-risk-plants.js (113 lines) and lives in src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants (set.js; journeys/linear with config.js, features/, flow/ and parties/; obligations/ with one file per section; services/commodities; spec/ with the decisions ledger; docs/ with recipe docs). Each page is a feature folder under journeys/linear/features holding page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, often fields.js, evaluation.js and a view-model folder, and one *.fit.spec.js (in-process page test). The journey order is flow/flow.js: start (dashboard), commodity (commodity type, commodities list), commodityDetails (commodity details sub-page), origin, arrival (arrival status, arrival details), destination (place of destination), parties (consignor, identification numbers), contact (consignment contact), and review (check answers, declaration, confirmation), with the hub (task list) and the dashboard's row actions (delete notification, cancel or amend) outside the sections. Feature folders are 100 to 1,300 lines each with their fit spec; the in-scope code, templates, copy and fit specs come to roughly 14,000 lines, plus the 1,433-line spec/decisions.json ledger (84 decisions). src/server/app/shared (about 940 lines outside its tests) holds layout.njk, kit.js, save-actions.njk, section-caption.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, set-context.js, paths.js and the shared copy (copy.js, copy-leaves.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js). The scope leaves out: unit tests (*.test.js, which repeat what the controllers and fit specs show), the journey platform outside the set and shared folders (engine/, flow/, bridge/, model/, services/persistence/, analysis/, auth/), sets/high-risk-plants/docs (developer recipes), and spec/journey-spec.json, spec/conflicts.json, spec/backlog-extras.json and spec/panel/ (the panel's evidence; spec/panel/README.md says decisions.json is the only place a ruling lives). It is cut into 9 parts by what a user sees: shared layout and kit, the flow and hub, the dashboard with its row actions, the commodity pages, origin and arrival, destination and consignor pickers, identification numbers and contact, the review pages, and the decisions ledger.

Extracted in 9 parts:
Part 1, Shared layout, kit, save actions and copy: Part 1 read, in full, the 15 files of the shared chrome and the set's mount: src/server/app/shared/layout.njk (130 lines: GOV.UK template with head, pageTitle, header, service navigation, phase banner, back link, notification banners, journey strip, journeyContent block and footer), kit.js (316 lines: shared copy resolution, surfaces, journey strip, error summary and field error builders, exit/change/run navigation targets, base and server-wide view-model chrome, recoverable save, stale-action redirect, page route pair, date reading and date field builder), save-actions.njk (the save-and-continue / save-and-return / cancel controls), section-caption.njk, error-summary.njk, error.njk, set-context.js (219 lines: set mounts, path-to-set resolution, request set context, required seams), paths.js (route shapes and prefixed links), copy.js and copy-leaves.js (locale resolution and the copy-leaf convention), copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (every shared string and validator default, English and machine-draft Welsh), sets/high-risk-plants/set.js (set id and base), journeys/linear/config.js (templates folder, layout, session cookie names) and routes-high-risk-plants.js (113 lines: the set's plugin registration, set-context hooks, journey flow configuration, entry guard and route mount). It covered: the page chrome (title pattern, header, service navigation and its four signed-in items, alpha phase banner, back link, notification banners for recoverable errors and stale actions, journey strip, footer links), the absence of a language toggle and breadcrumbs, the kit's behaviours every page shares (error summary, inline errors, save-and-return to the overview, change-from-check-answers return, opening-run navigation, session auth on every page route, stale-action redirect, recoverable save, date field format), the save actions macro and its rule for which pages show the return controls, the section caption, error summary and error page templates, every shared copy string in English and its Welsh counterpart, the validator default messages, and the set's id, mount, URL shapes, layout, session cookie names, entry guard and boot-time configuration checks. Unit tests (*.test.js) were not read, as the partition excludes them. One lookup outside the read list (src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js, by grep) confirmed where the layout's addressBookUrl, activeNavigationItem and staleActionRejected values come from; claims resting on it are inferred and say so.
Part 2, Journey flow, run, task rows and hub: Part 2 read, in full, the high-risk plants journey wiring under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear: flow/flow.js (the 9 sections and FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, with the ordering rationale in its comment), flow/run.js (RUN_STEPS, the opening run, and nextRunTarget), flow/task-rows.js (7 task rows and rowStatus), flow/entry-guard.js (the deep-link guard), flow/section-captions/index.js with its English and Welsh copy (5 caption sections), features/index.js (13 dispatch pages and 17 route groups), features/evaluation.js (10 evaluation bindings), the hub feature (controller.js with its 4 GROUPS and status tags, template.njk, copy.en.js and copy.cy.js), hub.fit.spec.js (12 tests), section-caption.fit.spec.js (2 tests), obligations/index.js (25 obligations in the set) and src/server/app/routes-high-risk-plants.js (how the set mounts and wires the flow). To word the hub's blocked-row and row-entry behaviour, the platform helpers it calls were glanced at (shared/paths.js for route paths, flow/navigation.js for rowEntry/rowGatePasses/sectionEntry, bridge/status for the five status values, flow/run-state.js for the run record); claims resting on them say so in the ref. It covers the page order, the opening run and where Continue goes after each step, every task row and how its status is worked out, the entry guard and what fires it, every section caption in English and Welsh, the Overview hub page (route, heading, groups, rows, status tags, button and back link, copy in both languages) with every fit test, and the registered routes, dispatch pages and obligation list. Each section's own pages and obligation section files are left to the parts that own them.
